title: Lefschetz–Verdier trace comparison
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum and the coefficient conventions
[def-weil-finite-field-fiber], [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], with
$A=A_{E,n}$ and $s=\Spec k$. Let $X$ be a proper finite-type $s$-scheme
[def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] and let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$.
Let $c=(c_1,c_2):C\to X\times_sX$ together with
$u:Lc_2^*K\to Rc_1^!K$ be an admissible cohomological correspondence
[def-trf-correspondence], [def-trf-admissibility]. Assume $c_2$ is proper
and the fixed scheme $F=\operatorname{Fix}(c)$ is proper over $s$ and has
finitely many open-and-closed connected components, in the sense of
[def-trf-fixed-scheme]. Then
$$
\operatorname{tr}_A\bigl(T_c(u)\mid R\Gamma_c(X,K)\bigr)
=\sum_{\beta\in\pi_0(F)}\operatorname{LT}_\beta(u)\quad\text{in }A,
$$
where $T_c(u)$ is the global operator of [def-trf-global-operator],
$\operatorname{tr}_A$ is the categorical trace of
[def-trf-categorical-trace], and $\operatorname{LT}_\beta(u)$ is the local
term on the component $\beta$ of [def-trf-local-term]. Thus the sum is over
clopen connected components of the fixed scheme; it is a sum over individual
fixed points when those components are reduced points.

external.place: (Source: the Lefschetz–Verdier trace formula for cohomological correspondences; see Milne, Lectures on Etale Cohomology, Section 29 (the Lefschetz fixed-point formula for nonconstant sheaves), with Section 25 for the constant-sheaf case, and $SGA5$, Expose III.

(Source: the Lefschetz–Verdier trace formula for cohomological correspondences; see Milne, Lectures on Etale Cohomology, Section 29 (the Lefschetz fixed-point formula for nonconstant sheaves), with Section 25 for the constant-sheaf case, and $SGA5$, Expose III.

proof.text:
The proper ordinary leg $c_2$ defines the endomorphism $T_c(u)$ of $R\Gamma_c(X,K)$ by [def-trf-global-operator]. Apply [lem-trf-global-operator-perfect] with the given admissible correspondence and $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$: this endomorphism lies in $D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A)$, which denotes perfect ring complexes for [def-trf-categorical-trace], so its categorical trace is defined. All hypotheses of [thm-trf-fixed-point-localization] hold: the same finite coefficient ring and geometric base, $X$ proper and finite type, $c$ admissible, $c_2$ proper, $F$ proper and $K$ finite-Tor constructible. Hence
$$\operatorname{tr}_A(T_c(u)\mid R\Gamma_c(X,K))=\int_F\operatorname{Tr}_c(u).$$
By [def-trf-trace-class], the class on the right is a morphism $\tau=\operatorname{Tr}_c(u):A_F\to\omega_{F,A}$.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph and first displayed identity

proof.text:
By [def-trf-fixed-scheme], the component hypothesis gives the finite disjoint union $F=\coprod_{\beta\in\pi_0(F)}\beta$, with inclusions $j_\beta$ open and closed. Each $\beta$ is a closed subscheme of the proper $F$, so [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper](c), applied to $j_\beta:\beta\hookrightarrow F$ and $F\to s$, makes $\beta$ proper over $s$. In particular $F$ and the components are separated finite type, as required in [lem-trf-integration-component-sum]. Apply that lemma to $T=F$, $B=\pi_0(F)$ and the section $\tau$ from step 1 to obtain
$$\int_F\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)=\sum_{\beta\in\pi_0(F)}\int_\beta(\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)|_\beta).$$
The lemma specifies restriction via $Lj_\beta^*$, the open-immersion identification with $Rj_\beta^!$ and the dualizing-composition identification, and explicitly states that these are the restrictions used for the local terms. For empty $F$ its empty-index clause gives the value $0$.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph; properness uses Stacks Tags 01W5 (lemma-closed-immersion-proper) and 01W3 (lemma-composition-proper), morphisms.tex

proof.text:
For each $\beta$, [def-trf-local-term] defines
$$\operatorname{LT}_\beta(u)=\int_\beta(\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)|_\beta).$$
Substitute this equality term by term in the finite sum of step 2 and substitute the result into the equality of step 1. This gives exactly the asserted trace identity in $A$. No assertion that the components are points is used.

proof_origin.place: Complete three-paragraph proof, with the closed-component properness lemma made explicit

blueprint_update.statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum
and the coefficient
conventions, $A=A_{E,n}$, $s=\Spec k$, and let $X$ be a
proper finite-type scheme.
Let $c=(c_1,c_2):C\to X\times_sX$ be an
admissible
cohomological correspondence with
$c_2$ proper and with
fixed scheme
$F=\operatorname{Fix}(c)$ proper over $s$ and with finitely many
open-and-closed components. Let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$. Then

$$
\operatorname{tr}_A\bigl(T_c(u)\mid R\Gamma_c(X,K)\bigr)
=
\sum_{\beta\in\pi_0(F)}
\operatorname{LT}_\beta(u)
\quad\text{in }A,
$$

where $T_c(u)$ is the
global operator of
[def-trf-global-operator],
$\operatorname{tr}_A$ the
categorical trace, and the
$\operatorname{LT}_\beta(u)$ are the
local terms. Equivalently, the
categorical trace of the global operator equals the sum of the local
terms over the fixed points.

proof.text:
The categorical trace on the left is defined because the global
operator $T_c(u)$ of [def-trf-global-operator] is a morphism of
$D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A)$, hence an endomorphism of a perfect complex,
by [lem-trf-global-operator-perfect]. With this, the
localization theorem [thm-trf-fixed-point-localization] gives

$$
\operatorname{tr}_A(T_c(u)\mid R\Gamma_c(X,K))
=\int_F\operatorname{Tr}_c(u).
$$

The component integration formula
[lem-trf-integration-component-sum] (applicable since each component
$\beta$, being closed in the proper $F$, is proper over $s$) rewrites
the right side as

$$
\sum_{\beta\in\pi_0(F)}
\int_\beta\bigl(\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)|_\beta\bigr).
$$

Each summand is $\operatorname{LT}_\beta(u)$ by
[def-trf-local-term], which proves the comparison.
